high.title: US Inflation Specter Threatens: Government Sells Bonds with Highest Yield in 19 Years, Market Shaken by 80% Probability Fed Raises Interest Rates
high.summary: US Treasury issued $25 billion in 30-year bonds at 5.046% yield - the highest in 19 years - following wholesale inflation data showing 6% rise in April, the highest since 2022. Middle East conflict is driving energy costs to record levels, creating inflation pressures that threaten long-term debt. Producer Price Index (PPI) jumped significantly above March's 4.3% and exceeded expectations at 3% forecast. This has major implications for Vietnamese bond markets and VND as US yield spikes typically strengthen the dollar and create capital outflow pressures from emerging markets. Vietnam's government bond yields may face upward pressure, and SBV may need to monitor FX stability more closely. Markets are pricing 80% probability of Fed rate hikes, which could tighten global liquidity conditions affecting Vietnam's capital flows and currency stability.

high.title: Vietnam to Have First Bank Exceeding 110,000 Billion VND Charter Capital, But Not From "Big 4"
high.summary: Techcombank (TCB) approved plan to increase charter capital from 70.862 trillion VND to 113.739 trillion VND through issuing 4.29 billion new shares, including 4.25 billion shares from retained earnings (60% ratio) and 35.9 million ESOP shares at 10,000 VND each. If successful, TCB will become Vietnam's largest bank by charter capital, surpassing Vietcombank, MB, VPBank, VietinBank and BIDV. This massive capital increase signals strong confidence in Vietnam's banking sector growth and could enhance TCB's lending capacity significantly. The move reflects the ongoing consolidation and strengthening of Vietnam's private banking sector, potentially impacting competitive dynamics in the credit market and supporting broader economic growth through expanded lending capacity.

high.title: State Bank Wants to Revise Regulations Related to Trillions of VND in Banking System, Experts Worried About Impact on Profitability and Credit Growth
high.summary: SBV proposes replacing key Circular 22/2019 on banking safety ratios, transitioning from Loan-to-Deposit ratio (LDR) to Credit-to-Deposit ratio (CDR) and introducing Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) to replace short-term funding for long-term loans ratio. The new CDR controls credit growth based on actual deposits from retail market only, excluding interbank funding from capital calculations. This represents a shift toward Basel III compliance and could significantly constrain credit expansion for banks heavily reliant on wholesale funding. Experts worry this could impact bank profitability and overall credit growth, potentially slowing economic expansion. The changes aim to improve banking system stability but may reduce liquidity in the interbank market and force banks to compete more intensively for retail deposits, potentially pushing up deposit rates.

medium.title: Vietnam Soon to Have Additional Bank Reaching 3 Trillion VND Assets, SHB and HDBank Preparing to Touch New Milestone
medium.summary: BIDV maintains largest asset base at 3.388 trillion VND, while VietinBank approaches the 3 trillion milestone with 2.924 trillion VND assets, needing only 76,000 billion more. Banking sector shows strong balance sheet expansion in Q1/2026, indicating robust credit demand and economic growth momentum supporting asset growth across major banks.

medium.title: Banking Revenue Race: BIDV Loses Crown, VPBank Rises to Match Big4 Level
medium.summary: Total banking sector revenue reached 190,371 billion VND in Q1/2026, up 15% YoY. BIDV lost its traditional revenue leadership position as VPBank emerged as strong competitor matching Big4 performance levels. Revenue redistribution among banks reflects changing competitive dynamics and market share shifts in Vietnamese banking sector.

medium.title: One Bank's Assets Decrease by Over 57,000 Billion VND
medium.summary: Sacombank's total assets fell 57,548 billion VND (6.3%) in Q1/2026 to 859.572 trillion VND, primarily due to reducing interbank deposits from 171.012 trillion to 113.369 trillion VND. This significant deleveraging suggests potential liquidity management strategy or regulatory compliance, indicating tighter interbank market conditions.

medium.title: Afternoon May 13: Both Gold Bar and Gold Ring Prices Decline
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices fell 500,000 VND/tael to 162.0-165.0 million VND range following international gold decline to around $4,700/ounce. Global gold weakness reflects reduced safe-haven demand amid Middle East diplomatic developments and rising US interest rate expectations affecting precious metals demand.

medium.title: SJC Gold and Plain Gold Ring Prices Morning May 14
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices continued declining on May 14 following global trends. SJC gold bars traded at 162-165 million VND/tael while gold rings ranged 161.8-165 million VND/tael. International gold faced second consecutive session decline due to inflation concerns reducing rate cut expectations.

medium.title: Vietcombank, VietinBank, Agribank, BIDV Suspend All Cash Withdrawal/Transfer Transactions for 5 Following Cases
medium.summary: Major banks implement new SBV regulations (Circulars 17/2024 and 18/2024) requiring complete customer data and biometric updates. Customers without updated ID documents and biometric data face transaction suspensions across all channels including counter, online, and ATM services, reflecting enhanced security and anti-money laundering compliance.
